Independently solved γ*=0.2625828410491615 and checked endpoint atoms fixed. For any stationary Borel probability, bounded truncated log h_M= max(log x,−M) with h_M(0)=−M has expected nonnegative drift by Jensen on lower branch x≤1/2. This drift is bounded and supported only at 0<x<e^-M/γ*, so its integral against any finite μ tends to zero by continuity from above. Right-branch drift ≤0, strictly negative uniformly on J_ε=[1/2+ε,1−ε]; stationarity then forces μ((1/2,1))=0. Every x∈(0,1/2], including left-branch x=1/2, has positive probability to reach upper branch within finite steps by an open word with β∈(3/2,7/4); stationarity and a countable union force μ((0,1/2])=0. Only δ0 and δ1 mixtures remain, and both are stationary. The result concerns finite stationary Borel probabilities, not sigma-finite or pathwise asymptotics.
